chunks: And from him (Al-Shaykh) from Al-Jarimi from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamzah and Durasht from Ibn Muskān from Al-Halabi who said:
I scratched my head while I was in iḥrām, so lice fell from it. I wanted to put them back, so he forbade me and said, 'Give a handful of food as charity.'

key_terms.مُحْرِمٌ: One in the state of iḥrām, wearing specific garments for Hajj or Umrah

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for scratching the head and losing lice while in iḥrām?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* illustrates the specific expiation (*kaffārah*) for accidentally removing hair or lice while in *iḥrām*, highlighting the Shia juristic preference for feeding the poor as a compensatory act. It underscores the principle that minor, unintentional breaches of ritual state require material restitution rather than complex ritual penalties, reflecting the practical application of *fiqh* in daily pilgrim life.
